artifacts.summary: Five-phase plan: extract the /todo health probe into an executable, fixture-testable script; reconcile the state schema's build_errors typing and status enum; rewrite todo.md's Sync Repository Metrics stage and delete the dead frontmatter step; register and deploy.

memory_candidates.content: Executable logic embedded as bash/jq snippets inside markdown command files is executed by an agent but never compiled, so defects accumulate invisibly and cannot be regression-tested. Confirmed instance: a state-write jq filter referencing an undefined $build_errors binding (only --arg errors was passed) fails with 'jq: 1 compile error', yet live state.json showed the write succeeding -- the executing agent had been silently repairing the binding at runtime, masking the defect indefinitely. The general pattern: when a defect's fix must be provable by an executed test, first extract the logic out of instruction prose into a real script with a JSON output contract, then make the command file a call site. Testability is the architectural driver, not code cleanliness. A second, compounding failure mode in the same class: a probe written as 'if cmd_a || cmd_b || true; then X else Y fi' makes the else branch structurally unreachable, so the metric it computes is a constant that no reader notices because the code looks like a real check.
